name: Evidence / data / experimental interpretation
objective: Use observations, measurements, data or experimental design to support a warranted conclusion while respecting uncertainty and alternative explanations.
choose_when: The main challenge is interpreting data or observations, designing a fair test, identifying variables or controls, or judging what evidence supports.
do_not_choose_when: Do not use when a graph or table merely presents already-determined values and no evidential inference or experimental decision is required.

slots.X: the evidence feature, variable, control, uncertainty or comparison that determines what may be inferred
slots.Y: a demonstrated principle of fair comparison, measurement, trend interpretation or causal inference
slots.Z: the evidential inference or design move that connects the observations to a warranted claim
slots.W: the learner's conclusion, experimental choice or evaluation of what the evidence does and does not show

hint_objectives.REPRESENTATION: Clarify which observation, variable or comparison matters and what is actually measured rather than assumed.
hint_objectives.KEY_CONCEPT: Correlate X with a known fair-test, measurement or inference principle Y.
hint_objectives.CRUX: Open the warranted inference or design route Z while leaving the evidential conclusion or design decision W to the learner.

figure_policy.job: Use the actual graph, table, apparatus or data view when it is part of the evidence. Preserve uncertainty, axes, units and controls; do not annotate the conclusion into the evidence.

misconception_families: precision or uncertainty treated as exact truth
